tasks.short: Help site managers and department heads with cost questions, cost allocation and their yearly budget.

today.trigger: A site manager, the Finance Director or a budget holder asks a cost or allocation question, or the yearly budget round starts in September.
steps: Read the question in Outlook or Teams and work out which cost centres and periods it touches
Pull GL actuals from AFAS Profit or the Power BI extract into Excel
Build or adjust an allocation (warehouse space, pallet moves, FTE) for shared costs such as the Tilburg DC overhead
Write a short answer or walk the budget holder through the template in a call
Update the SharePoint budget file once they agree
drudgery: Re-extracting the same GL data for every question
Re-explaining the budget template and allocation keys every year
Chasing the latest version of a file across mail threads
today.time_sinks: Collecting data and rebuilding allocation sheets for each request, not the advice itself.

lenses.faster: A copilot on the Power BI model answers 'what did Venlo spend on forklift lease per pallet' in minutes, so the analyst starts from numbers instead of extracting them.
lenses.autonomous: When the budget round opens, each budget holder gets a pre-filled template with last year's actuals, CAO wage step and known contracts already in.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets cost-to-serve per client and per shift, not just per cost centre, so allocation advice becomes a regular service.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding the same allocation sheet; time goes to the conversation about what drives the cost.
lenses.options: For an allocation question the copilot shows three keys side by side (square metres, pallet moves, labour hours) with the effect on each site.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the allocation rules and the Q&A layer on the data model, and checks its answers rather than producing each one.
reach: Controller: maintaining cost-centre allocation keys
HR Business Partner: workforce cost questions from site managers

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which allocation is fair and defensible to site managers, and saying no to a budget holder with context.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions are open and the advice carries judgment and relationships; AI speeds up data retrieval and drafting while the analyst leads.

in_practice.trigger: Question from a budget holder in Teams or mail, or opening of the budget round.
steps: Copilot queries the Power BI/AFAS semantic model for the relevant cost centres
It drafts an answer with figures, the allocation key used and assumptions
Analyst checks figures and wording, adjusts the key if needed
Analyst sends the answer or discusses it in a short call
Pre-filled budget templates are generated in SharePoint for the budget round
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews every number and recommendation before it goes to a budget holder.
data_needed: GL actuals by cost centre and site
Allocation keys (m2, pallet moves, labour hours)
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint FP&A Q&A log with question, answer and data source

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI answers natural-language questions over a semantic model.
Copilot in Excel can build formulas and summaries from tables.
AFAS Profit exposes GL data through GetConnectors for automated extracts.

risks: Copilot answers from a wrongly modelled measure and nobody notices
Budget holders treat a draft answer as Finance's position
Allocation keys that are not agreed with site managers cause disputes
research_questions: Which share of questions over the last quarter could be answered from the existing Power BI model without new data?
Do site managers accept a written copilot-backed answer, or do they want a conversation anyway?
How accurate is Power BI Copilot on our model for ten real past questions?

tasks.short: Look at budgets against actuals over time to see trends that change what we need next year.

today.trigger: Monthly after close, and before the forecast update or budget round.
steps: Export actuals and budget by cost centre from Power BI to Excel
Build trend lines for main cost lines (agency labour, fuel, overtime, energy, rent)
Compare with volume drivers such as pallets, orders and trips
Note trends and likely causes in a sheet or slide
Discuss findings with the Controller or Finance Director
drudgery: Copying exports into the same Excel trend sheet every month
Manually lining up volume data with costs
today.time_sinks: Data prep and matching volumes to costs takes most of the time.

lenses.faster: Trend and unit-cost calculations run on the nightly refresh; the analyst only reviews flagged breaks and the drafted commentary.
lenses.autonomous: After each close a job computes unit costs per driver, flags trend breaks and drafts a commentary page in Power BI.
lenses.ambitious: Trends tracked per client contract and per site weekly, including flex labour from agency portals, so peak-season needs show up months earlier.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses pasting exports; what remains is finding the story behind a trend.
lenses.options: For each flagged trend the model gives two or three plausible drivers ranked by data fit, for the analyst to confirm.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the driver set and thresholds and checks the commentary quality.
reach: People Analytics: overtime and absence trends that drive labour cost
Controller: month-end variance commentary

tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a cost jump is a one-off client start or a structural change, from talking to the sites.
tasks.pattern_why: Trend maths is deterministic; an LLM turns flagged breaks plus context into checkable commentary inside that pipeline.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly Power BI refresh after month close is marked complete.
steps: Pipeline computes unit costs per driver and statistical trend breaks
LLM drafts commentary per flagged line with the numbers it used
Analyst confirms or corrects causes and adds site context
Approved commentary is published in the Power BI report
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each trend explanation before it is published.
data_needed: GL actuals and budget by cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Commentary table in the Power BI dataset with draft, final text and approver

evidence.claim: Power BI has anomaly detection on line charts and Copilot narrative summaries.
LLMs can draft variance commentary from tabular data that a person verifies.

risks: Volume data from warehouse systems is not in the AFAS extract
LLM invents a cause that sounds right
Too many flags make people ignore them
research_questions: Which volume drivers are available daily, and from which system?
How many of last year's trend explanations would the draft have got right?
What threshold keeps flags under about ten per month?

tasks.short: Go through monthly department cost reports and chase budget holders when they overspend.

today.trigger: Month close in AFAS Profit, usually working day 5 to 8.
steps: Run department reports in Power BI per cost centre
Spot overspends and unusual postings, check invoices in AFAS
Check agency invoices against ordered hours in the portals
Mail or Teams budget holders asking for explanations
Collect answers and report to the Controller
drudgery: Scanning dozens of cost centres line by line
today.time_sinks: Finding the posting behind an overspend and waiting for budget holder answers.

lenses.faster: Overspends above a threshold arrive already linked to the invoices and agency hours behind them.
lenses.autonomous: After close, an agent drafts a question to each budget holder with the overspend and its underlying postings, sent after analyst approval.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly instead of monthly control, so agency overspend in peak season is caught within the week.
lenses.joy: No more line-by-line scanning; the analyst handles the real issues.
lenses.options: For each overspend the agent proposes: accept, reclassify the posting, or ask for a forecast change.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets thresholds and rules and reviews the exception list.
reach: Bookkeeper: spotting miscoded invoices
Controller: first-pass review of month-end postings

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an overspend is acceptable and keeping a good working relation with budget holders.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems, exceptions and outgoing messages; a person approves before questions or reclassifications are acted on.

in_practice.trigger: Close flag set in AFAS Profit.
steps: Pull actuals vs budget per cost centre and apply thresholds
Drill each overspend to postings, invoices and agency hours
Draft a question per budget holder in Teams
Analyst approves, edits or drops each question
Track answers and update the control report
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every outgoing question and any proposed reclassification.
data_needed: Budget and actuals by cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of exceptions with status, answer and approver

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit data including invoices can be read via GetConnectors.
An agent can draft and track follow-up messages via Microsoft 365.

risks: Agency portals have no API, so hours must be scraped or exported
Budget holders feel watched if messages come too often
Wrong drill-down leads to a wrong accusation of overspend
research_questions: Do the three agency portals offer exports or APIs for hours and invoices?
What share of overspends last year were miscoding versus real overspend?
Will budget holders answer a templated Teams question as fast as a personal one?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions from departments for missing lines, wrong maths and breaking our budget rules.

today.trigger: Departments return budget templates during the yearly round or a forecast update.
steps: Collect Excel templates from SharePoint and mail
Check totals, formulas and that all cost lines are filled
Check wage costs against CAO scales and headcount in AFAS
Check against the budget guidelines (inflation, flex share, capex rules)
Send corrections back and log status
drudgery: Checking broken formulas and overwritten cells
Tracking which version is the latest
today.time_sinks: Manual cell-by-cell checks and rounds of corrections.

lenses.faster: A rule engine checks each submission on upload and returns a list of issues within minutes.
lenses.autonomous: On upload to SharePoint, checks run and the budget holder gets the issue list directly; only clean or disputed files reach the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Every forecast update, not only the yearly budget, gets the full check, including CAO wage steps and flex worker rates.
lenses.joy: No cell-hunting; the analyst discusses the assumptions that matter.
lenses.options: For a failed rule the tool shows the corrected figure and the effect on the total.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes and maintains the rule set and reviews disputed cases.
reach: Payroll Specialist: checking wage cost assumptions against CAO
Compensation and Benefits: salary increase assumptions

tasks.human_edge: Deciding when a rule exception is justified and negotiating it with the budget holder.
tasks.pattern_why: Completeness, maths and policy rules can be written down and checked on structured templates.

in_practice.trigger: Budget template uploaded to the SharePoint budget library.
steps: Validate structure, formulas and totals
Compare headcount and wage cost to AFAS and CAO tables
Apply budget guideline rules
Return issue list to the submitter and update status
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst decides on exceptions and signs off each submission as accepted.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint status list per submission with rule results

evidence.claim: Power Automate can trigger flows on SharePoint file upload.
Planning tools like Adaptive Planning enforce input validation in budget templates.

risks: Budget holders change template layouts and break the checks
Rules lag behind new CAO agreements
Personal salary data in templates needs AVG access control
research_questions: How many issue types were found in last year's submissions and can each be written as a rule?
Can templates be locked enough to keep structure stable?
Who maintains CAO tables after each new agreement?

tasks.short: Work out what a new project, client or site change will cost from our records and data.

today.trigger: Request for a business case: new client warehouse, extra shift, new fleet, automation project.
steps: Gather comparable costs from AFAS (labour, rent, equipment, agency rates)
Get volume and staffing assumptions from operations
Build a cost model in Excel
Check with the Controller and HR on wage and staffing costs
Present required budget to management
today.time_sinks: Collecting reference data and getting assumptions from operations.

lenses.faster: An agent assembles reference costs from past projects and sites and fills a standard cost model; the analyst tests assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: A new business-case request in the SharePoint list triggers a first draft model with reference data attached.
lenses.ambitious: Every client tender gets a proper cost-to-serve model, not only the big ones.
lenses.joy: Less searching, more time with operations on what will really happen on the floor.
lenses.options: Low, base and high cases on volume, flex share and wage increase by default.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the standard cost model and reference library.
reach: Sales or commercial: tender pricing support
HR Business Partner: staffing plan for new sites

tasks.human_edge: Challenging operations' assumptions and judging risk in a new client or site.
tasks.pattern_why: Several data sources and assumptions; output feeds a funding decision so a person must approve.

in_practice.trigger: Business case request logged in SharePoint.
steps: Agent pulls reference costs and rates from AFAS, Power BI and agency data
Agent fills the standard cost model with three scenarios
Analyst reviews assumptions with operations
Analyst finalises and presents
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off the model before it goes to management.
data_needed: Historical costs per site and client
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint business-case library with model versions

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel can help build scenario tables and formulas.
An agent can assemble reference costs across systems for a cost model.

risks: Past costs do not fit a new type of operation
research_questions: How many business cases were done last year and how long did each take?
Is project or client cost data coded consistently in AFAS?
Would a standard cost model cover most requests?

tasks.short: Summarise budgets and advise yes or no on requests for extra money, like capex or extra flex staff.

today.trigger: A funds request arrives: capex, extra headcount, budget transfer.
steps: Read the request and supporting files
Check budget room and forecast in Excel/Power BI
Assess payback and alignment with plan
Write a recommendation memo
Send to Finance Director for decision
drudgery: Writing memos in the same format
today.time_sinks: Gathering budget room and writing the memo.

lenses.faster: The request comes with remaining budget, forecast effect and a draft memo already prepared.
lenses.autonomous: A request in the SharePoint form triggers the checks and draft memo; the analyst edits and recommends.
lenses.ambitious: All requests, including small ones, get a consistent check and a register of decisions.
lenses.joy: No memo formatting; the analyst focuses on the call.
lenses.options: The draft offers approve, approve partially, or defer, each with forecast effect.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets approval criteria and checks the register for patterns.
reach: Controller: maintaining authorisation matrix
HR Business Partner: headcount requests

tasks.human_edge: The recommendation itself and accountability for it; the Finance Director decides.
tasks.pattern_why: Multiple checks and a draft, but the recommendation and decision stay with people.

in_practice.trigger: Funds request submitted in a SharePoint form.
steps: Check budget room and forecast impact
Calculate payback where relevant
Draft memo with options
Analyst edits and recommends
Finance Director decides; register updated
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs the recommendation, Finance Director decides.
data_needed: Budget and forecast by cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint funds request register with decision and approver

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts documents from given sources.

risks: Headcount requests touch staffing, check with works council where the OR has rights
research_questions: How many requests per month and what share are small?
Does the Finance Director accept a standard memo format?
Which criteria are written down today?

tasks.short: Organise the regular monthly budget reports and one-off reports for management.

today.trigger: Monthly reporting calendar, or a management ad hoc request.
steps: Collect inputs from Controller and Accountants
Refresh Power BI and export to PowerPoint
Write commentary
Review with Finance Director
Distribute

lenses.faster: The pack builds itself from Power BI with draft commentary; the analyst reviews.
lenses.autonomous: After close the report is generated and sent for review automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Site-level packs for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo every month, not just a company pack.
lenses.joy: No slide formatting; time goes to the message.
lenses.options: Special reports start from a few draft layouts to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the report design and commentary standards.
reach: Controller: month-end reporting pack
People Analytics: HR cost section

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what management needs to hear and how to frame it.
tasks.pattern_why: Regular reports have fixed structure; generate from the model with an LLM commentary step.

in_practice.trigger: Close complete or ad hoc request.
steps: Refresh dataset and render paginated report
Insert approved commentary
Finance Director reviews
Distribute via Teams

evidence.claim: Power BI paginated reports and subscriptions deliver scheduled reports.

risks: Errors spread silently to all recipients
Special reports still need manual work
research_questions: Which reports are truly recurring and fixed?
How much time goes into special reports?

tasks.short: Make site and department budgets add up to the company total, including the contingency reserve.

today.trigger: Budget round and each forecast update or transfer.
steps: Roll up cost centre budgets to site and company level in Excel
Check totals against targets
Allocate contingency for peak season and risks
Fix mismatches with budget holders

lenses.faster: Roll-ups and reconciliation run automatically on the cost centre hierarchy.
lenses.autonomous: Every change triggers a check that totals still match targets and contingency rules.
lenses.ambitious: Contingency is sized from data on past peaks and risks, not a flat percentage.
lenses.options: Contingency scenarios for mild, normal and heavy peak season.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the hierarchy and contingency rules.
reach: Controller: hierarchy maintenance in AFAS

tasks.human_edge: Deciding contingency size and who gets it.
tasks.pattern_why: Hierarchies and roll-up rules are fully structured and checkable.

steps: Roll up by hierarchy
Check against targets and contingency rule
Flag mismatches

evidence.claim: Planning tools roll up budgets by hierarchy automatically.

risks: Hierarchy in AFAS and Excel differ
research_questions: Is the cost centre hierarchy the same in AFAS and the budget files?
How was contingency sized and used in past years?

role.altitude: The FP&A analyst stops building spreadsheets and runs the planning system: data pipelines from AFAS and agency portals, validation rules, driver models and the commentary standard, checking outputs and improving them.
reach: Controller: month-end variance commentary and allocation keys
People Analytics: workforce cost and overtime trends
HR Business Partner: headcount cost planning
Bookkeeper: miscoding detection
Credit and Collections: DSO forecasting
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in AFAS and agency portals and by trust; judgment, negotiation with budget holders and accountability for recommendations stay human. Realistic saving about half of the roughly 1,600 hours per FTE.
skills_to_grow: Power BI data modelling and DAX
Writing rules and checking AI output
role.ambitious_version: A rolling 18-month driver-based forecast per site and client, refreshed weekly, with peak-season flex scenarios and cost-to-serve per client, so Finance closes faster with a forecast the business trusts.
